pr_title: `EXPLAIN ANALYSE` should honor profiler output format
pr_body:
Today, the `EXPLAIN ANALYSE` statement always results in a query tree output, regardless of the profiler output format pragma. This commit makes it honor that setting.

To do so, the default output format had to be changed from `NONE` to `QUERY_TREE`, to avoid output from being suppressed by default. Note that we have another boolean that controls whether the profiler is on or not.

Closes #3094

Hopefully you're ok with it.

issue_context.title: Feature Request: way for `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` to return a JSON string instead of the ascii representation as a result set
issue_context.body:
# Problem Statement

Currently, `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` returns an ascii representation of the plan.

This is the perfect representation when someone is using duckdb in an _interactive environment_ such as a jupyter notebook. Usually the output you'd want from this kind of query is a flexible text-based representation that enables the data analyst to understand what the query is doing.

But for _programmatic_ use-cases, the ascii representation does not work. Instead of having a human in the loop analyzing the query, it's the _computer_ that needs an easy way to understand the query so that it can do things with the plan – for instance, do further analysis on the sources, analyze the scans and projections in different ways. Which likely means a JSON string is more appropriate.

There is a work-around we can employ. Setting these pragmas

```
PRAGMA enable_profiling=json;
PRAGMA profiling_output='./profile.json';
```

... and then reading back `profile.json` into one's application. But this is quite limited. Some of the assumptions of the work-around break down when my build target uses `duckdb-wasm` instead of the node client.

# Proposed Solution

A way to tell any client (WASM, Node, Python, R, etc.) that the output of an `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` query should return the same JSON returned by the `enable_profiling` pragma would be ideal. Defaulting to ascii seems like a great option to uphold the current expectation for interactive users.

A pragma-based approach would likely give maximum flexibility to users for myriad use-cases, including in the CLI. But I'm open to any solution that enables the computer to parse the JSON representation. It seems that `PRAGMA enable_profiling=json` could also apply to `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` but perhaps this breaks a mental model of interactive vs. programmatic in some way I haven't thought of.
